todo: Obtain qualified-human citation verification for the proposed Bell's palsy to keratitis association.
Confirm facial-nerve palsy with incomplete eyelid closure or ocular exposure, objective exposure-related corneal disease, chronology, and competing corneal causes before publication.

suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-35 adds this relationship only as a bounded facial-palsy exposure-keratopathy association. A 23-year retrospective ophthalmic review describes ocular sequelae among patients with facial palsy, but the clinical sample does not establish that every keratitis diagnosis in a person with Bell's palsy was caused by the palsy. Require independently documented Bell's palsy or facial-nerve palsy with incomplete eyelid closure or other documented ocular-surface exposure, and separately documented exposure keratopathy, corneal epithelial defect, ulcer, or a clinically defined keratitis phenotype with compatible chronology. Do not infer generic keratitis from facial palsy, facial weakness, eye discomfort, or redness alone. Preserve infectious, contact-lens, autoimmune, traumatic, postoperative, neurotrophic, medication-related, and other corneal causes.
evidenceGaps: Independent documentation of Bell's palsy or facial-nerve palsy, eyelid closure, corneal sensation, and ocular exposure
Ophthalmic examination documenting exposure keratopathy, epithelial defect, ulcer, or a compatible keratitis phenotype
Chronology connecting facial-nerve dysfunction and ocular-surface disease
Assessment of infectious, contact-lens, autoimmune, traumatic, postoperative, neurotrophic, medication-related, and other corneal causes
Ophthalmology and neurology assessment of the individual's phenotype and competing explanations

sourceReferences.citation: Joseph SS, Joseph AW, Smith JI, Niziol LM, Musch DC, Nelson CC. Evaluation of Patients with Facial Palsy and Ophthalmic Sequelae: A 23-Year Retrospective Review. Ophthalmic Epidemiology. 2017;24(5):341-345. PMID 28319442. doi:10.1080/09286586.2017.1294186.
sourceReferences.note: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-35 retrospective facial-palsy ophthalmic-sequelae evidence for the bounded exposure-keratopathy proposition. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source remains pending qualified-human review.
sourceReferences.sourceLocator: PMID 28319442; 23-year retrospective review of facial palsy and ophthalmic sequelae; approved ME-35 guard limits the broad keratitis target to objective exposure-related corneal disease.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: The facial-palsy ophthalmic review supports exposure-related ocular-surface complications as a possible sequela of facial-nerve dysfunction, without establishing an individual keratitis nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR section 3.310 is established; ocular exposure, objective corneal findings, chronology, and competing corneal causes require individual review.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Facial-nerve dysfunction may reduce eyelid closure and tear-film protection, allowing exposure-related epithelial injury and inflammation, but the individual's corneal disease mechanism remains hypothesized until ophthalmic findings and alternative causes are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: This relationship is supported as an association only. The retrospective facial-palsy review describes ophthalmic sequelae but does not prove that an individual's keratitis was caused by Bell's palsy.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Facial-nerve palsy and eyelid-closure findings; objective exposure-related corneal disease; chronology; and assessment of infectious, contact-lens, autoimmune, traumatic, postoperative, neurotrophic, medication-related, and other causes.
